review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. North Pacific survey models provide even/odd-year marine SST preference estimates; configured SST band is shifted warm, and seafloor depth is only a weak pelagic proxy.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 2-4 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for pink salmon.
factors.value_notes: Langan et al. (2024) estimated pink salmon marine preferred SST separately by brood-cycle parity: even-year 3.0-12.6 °C (80% HDI), core 4.3-9.4 °C, median 7.9 °C, modal 6.6 °C; odd-year 3.0-11.8 °C, core 4.3-8.9 °C, median 7.5 °C, modal 6.4 °C. The configured 6-15 °C range and 8-13 °C ideal are warmer and exclude much of the modeled cold-side preference. The parity distinction matters; these are North Pacific marine survey models, not local stock-specific catch curves.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for pink salmon.
factors.value_notes: Pink salmon spend their marine feeding phase in pelagic North Pacific waters and migrate back to coastal rivers to spawn. NOAA notes that fishing gear targeting them rarely contacts the ocean floor. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth; no reviewed source validates a universal 0-50 m bottom-depth preference. Retain as a weak coastal/shelf proxy only.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.
